hook.context: South Asian women aged 45+ with BMI below 25 in Chennai, Delhi and Karachi, compared with US white women.
hook.question: Think a 'normal' BMI rules out diabetes?
hook.opener: Chai break at the office, and someone brings up blood sugar.
hook.prompt: Guess: how did diabetes rates compare?

reveals.label: higher risk of diabetes
reveals.sentence: South Asian women aged 45 and over in Chennai, Delhi and Karachi with BMI under 25 kg/m2 had a 5.3 times higher risk of diabetes than US whites.

qualifiers: A comparison between groups in one study, not a prediction for you.
hook.quote: Similarly, in women, the risk of diabetes in those with BMI <25 kg/m2 was 5.3 times higher in South Asian (IRR (95% CI) 5.27 (3.64 to 7.54)) and 2.5 times higher in US blacks (IRR (95% CI) 2.36 (1.56 to 3.78)) as compared with US whites.

source.full: Narayan KMV, Kondal D, Daya N et al. Incidence and pathophysiology of diabetes in South Asian adults living in India and Pakistan compared with US blacks and whites. BMJ Open Diabetes Research & Care, 2021.

rounds.question: After stopping a weight management medicine, how fast does weight come back each month?
rounds.opener: On the bus home, a reel about weight medicines pops up on the phone.

reveals.label: monthly rate of weight regain
reveals.sentence: On average, the monthly rate of weight regain was 0.4 kg (95% CI 0.3 to 0.5).

qualifiers: An average across studies, not a prediction for you.
All weight-management medicines, not only GLP-1.
rounds.quote: The average monthly rate of weight regain was 0.4 kg (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.3 to 0.5)

source.full: West S, Scragg J, Aveyard P et al. Weight regain after cessation of medication for weight management: systematic review and meta-analysis. BMJ, 2026.

rounds.question: On these medicines, does the amount of lean mass in kilograms go up, down or stay the same?
rounds.opener: Morning in the neighbourhood park, and a friend asks about sugar tests.

reveals.label: Absolute lean mass changed
reveals.sentence: Absolute lean mass changed by −1.74 kg on average.

qualifiers: Results varied a lot between studies.
rounds.quote: However, a signiﬁcant decrease was observed in the absolute change in lean mass (−1.74 kg; 95% CI: −3.04 to −0.45; p < 0.00001; I² = 98%)

source.full: Laverde LP, Muñoz-Velandia OM, Alfonso D et al. Effect of GLP-1 receptor agonists at doses for obesity management on muscle health: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). International Journal of Obesity, 2026.

rounds.question: And lean mass as a share of body weight: up, down or the same?
rounds.opener: A cousin's wedding, and the aunties are comparing health reports.

reveals.label: Lean mass as a share of total weight rose
reveals.sentence: Lean mass as a share of total weight rose by 1.81% on average.

qualifiers: The authors advise nutrition and exercise alongside treatment.
rounds.quote: Seven studies (821 patients) were included in the analysis. GLP1-RA signiﬁcantly improved lean mass as a proportion of total weight, with an observed increase of 1.81% (95% CI: 1.1– 2.52; p < 0.00001; I² = 7%).

source.full: Laverde LP, Muñoz-Velandia OM, Alfonso D et al. Effect of GLP-1 receptor agonists at doses for obesity management on muscle health: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). International Journal of Obesity, 2026.

rounds.question: Which kind of side effect was most common in these trials?
rounds.opener: Family dinner at home, and the talk turns to health check-ups.

reveals.label: Mostly stomach and gut side effects
reveals.sentence: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation were the most common gastrointestinal adverse effects.

qualifiers: These findings are about this class of medicines, not one product.
A doctor weighs the benefits against the side effects for each person.
rounds.quote: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation were the most common gastrointestinal adverse effects.

source.full: Ismaiel A, Scarlata GGM, Boitos I et al. Gastrointestinal adverse events associated with GLP-1 RA in non-diabetic patients with overweight or obesity: a systematic review and network meta-analysis. International Journal of Obesity, 2025.

gap_cards.title: Is this only for diabetics?
gap_cards.body: Our papers don't answer this well. Ask a doctor about it, with your own history.
gap_cards.opener: Tea with the neighbours on the balcony, and someone asks who these medicines are for.
gap_cards.context: This review looked at non-diabetic subjects with overweight or obesity.
